title: A littleEaster color.
summary: An Easter family visit to Berlin Farms in Massachusetts: colorful eggs, an enthusiastic bunny, wide-open fields and a few practical notes before you go.

A spring visit to Berlin FarmsA littleEaster color.An egg hunt, a bunny with a few good poses, and a family photograph worth keeping.An AUsome Life · Published October 7, 2026From an earlier Easter visitPastel eggs across the lawn. White fences beyond the buildings. One orange jacket that had apparently declined the pastel dress code.Our Easter photographs from Berlin Farms deserved a little space in the journal. The family storyMap & visit detailsAccess & sensory notesMore photographs Opened from the family albumThe eggs were everywhere.There is a particular sort of New England spring photograph: green beginning to return to the grass, bare trees in the distance, and everybody sensibly still wearing a jacket. Our Berlin Farms pictures have all of that, with the addition of a lawn covered in pink, yellow, blue and green eggs.A canvas shopping bag is ready for the egg hunt. The Easter Bunny has a pink bow, a floral backdrop, and considerably more enthusiasm for posing than most adults can sustain. I especially like the photograph with the arms up. There is plenty happening in it, and that smile is the part I keep coming back to.Then there is the family picture: the three of us together, the bunny at one end, and the stone patio beneath our feet. I am glad we have that one. A canvas tote, a lawn full of eggs, and a very visible orange jacket.All of us in the frame. The bunny makes four. A little spring color. Original editorial illustration.Between the photographsA little room to look around.The farm makes a lovely setting for this chapter. White clapboard buildings sit beside lines of white fencing, with fields stretching beyond them. In one photograph, a horse is grazing in the distance. The colors are mostly green, white and gray, which leaves the orange jacket with very little competition.I like having a wider view among the close-ups. It brings back the shape of a place: the deck, the fence, the buildings around the egg-hunt lawn. A family album needs a little of the scenery, too. White fences, open fields, and a sky still considering its spring options. One for the albumThe good partis right here.The photographs beside the black door are worth keeping in the set. There is a cap being adjusted, a yellow egg on the grass, and four very large letters spelling LOVE. The farm has helpfully supplied the caption.A tote bag, a bunny, and a few photographs I am glad we took.That is what I want to keep from this Easter visit: the color on the lawn, the bunny pictures, and our family together in the middle of it.One more photograph beside the LOVE door. Read the complete instructions.The details left inThe useful part, in full.Open just what you need.Put today’s plan first.+A useful handover helps the next person act. Begin with today’s date, the agreed time together, what the person is expecting and anything that has changed. Keep the long history in its appropriate record. Make the plan with the person receiving support, using the communication they prefer and any assistance they need. Explain who is arriving, what is happening and how the visit will finish. Offer choices within the arrangements that are genuinely available. Before responsibility changes hands Confirm the incoming person has arrived and has agreed to take over.Review the important changes and invite questions.Check they can access the needed supplies, contacts and current instructions.Confirm what happens if plans change or the return is delayed. When support needs uninterrupted coverage, do not rely on an unanswered message as a completed handoff. Show how communication works today.+Have the person’s usual communication tools available and ready to use, including a familiar backup if they have one. Show the incoming supporter where they are kept and explain any practical help needed to use them. Do not replace a familiar system with a new worksheet simply because the worksheet is convenient. Share the useful basics: how the person makes a choice, asks for help, signals a pause and indicates that they want to finish. If a signal is uncertain, say so. “This sometimes means a break; check with them” is more useful than presenting a guess as a fixed fact. The NJC Communication Bill of Rights supports meaningful choices, direct communication and access to working communication systems. The practical goal here is that the person can still participate when their usual supporter is away. Keep current care instructions alongside the short note.+The handover is a summary of arrangements, not a substitute for the person’s current care, medical or emergency plans. Confirm that the incoming supporter is authorized, trained where necessary and able to provide the support being transferred. Give them access to the actual instructions and essential information they need, through the established private channel. Do not omit a critical safety detail merely to keep the summary to one page. Equally, do not improvise medication directions, eating or drinking instructions, lifting methods or emergency procedures in this template. If instructions conflict, are out of date or cannot be accessed, resolve the issue with the appropriate person before the affected activity or handoff. Follow the existing emergency arrangements for urgent situations. The short handover template.+Use these headings in the private record or on the paper system you already use. The blank version is deliberately general. Add only the information appropriate for this recipient and setting; keep completed copies secure. Date and timePrepared: ______ · Support begins: ______ · Expected finish: ______ Today’s agreed planFirst: ______ · Then: ______ · The shorter version: ______ The person’s choicesWhat they have chosen: ______ · What is still open: ______ CommunicationTools and location: ______ · Useful partner guidance: ______ · Backup: ______ Food, drink and ordinary suppliesWhat is ready: ______ · Where the relevant current instructions are kept: ______ A pause or finishHow to check: ______ · Available place or option: ______ Changes that matter todayConfirmed changes: ______ · Question to resolve before handoff: ______ Current care and emergency instructionsPrivate location and version/date: ______ · Access checked: ______ Contacts and changes of planAgreed contact route: ______ · Backup route: ______ · Return-delay plan: ______ Responsibility acceptedOutgoing supporter: ______ · Incoming supporter: ______ · Time confirmed: ______ A completed handover can contain private information. Do not put it on a public noticeboard, leave it in a shared vehicle or paste it into an open online tool. Use the person’s agreed permissions and the provider’s requirements for storage and sharing. What a useful note sounds like.+Illustrative example: “Today we agreed on the library and home. The shorter version is returning the books only. The communication bag is beside the coat and has been checked. Please confirm the current return time with me before I leave.” This example does not contain the safety instructions for a real person. Those still need to be accessible to the person providing support. Close the handover at the other end.+Before leaving, give a brief factual update: what took place, what changed, anything needing attention and who has agreed to the next step. Complete required records in the proper system. Confirm that the next supporter has accepted responsibility where continuous support is needed. Revise the standing information when something changes. Remove an outdated copy so it cannot be mistaken for the current plan.
